messages:
sam: Customer (AcmeCorp) emailed security@redwood with a potential data exposure claim. They say they observed outbound traffic from an IP they believe belongs to our fleet into their S3 bucket and are requesting immediate containment.

lina: Can you paste the snippet from their email and any headers? timestamps?

sam: Snippet: 'Observed connection from 18.204.5.12 -> s3://acme-logs on 2026-03-19T21:12Z. Attached pcap.' No headers in the email, but they attached a pcap.

emma (sec-oncall): Jumping in. Which deployment is this for the customer — hosted, dedicated, or private?

sam: It's Dedicated in us-west-2. Tenant id: tenant-acme-7. They said they have VPC peering with our dedicated nodes.

dave (infra): Ok. First checks: confirm whether any of our dedicated nodes had egress to that bucket. Look at VPC flow logs and node-level logs. I'll run queries against flow logs for that timeframe.

emma: I'm pulling network flows for tenant-acme-7 from 2026-03-19T20:30 -> 2026-03-19T22:00. Also grabbing pod/network namespace lists.

sec-bot: audit: started collection: vpc-flowlogs (tenant-acme-7, 2026-03-19T20:30-22:00), node logs, container stdout/stderr.

lina: Customer also asked for KMS decrypt logs. They want assurance that keys weren't used to decrypt anything.

sam: They mentioned IP 18.204.5.12 specifically in the pcap. That looks like an ephemeral host in our public pool — could be different tenant traffic NAT'd.

dave: Quick hypothesis: internal backup or export job may have posted to their bucket using a presigned URL. Check job history for any backup jobs around 21:10-21:15.

emma: Forensics note: collect process lists, open sockets, and kernel audit logs from the tenant's containers. Also snapshot disks before making changes.

sec-bot: rbac-audit: queried RBAC events for tenant-acme-7 for last 48h. No new service principals or role bindings found.

sam: Customer wants us to pull KMS logs (Decrypt events) and provide the times. Lina, can you query CloudTrail for Decrypt events filtered by keyId or tenant tag?

lina: Running cloudtrail lookup: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-19T20:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T22:30:00Z --region us-west-2.

sec-bot: cloudtrail query result: 2 Decrypt events at 2026-03-19T21:12:17Z and 2026-03-19T21:12:42Z from source IP 18.204.5.12 using assumed-role arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-deployer-role/session. Events reference KeyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:...:key/abcd-tenant-acme-7.

emma: If Decrypt events are from our deployer role, that may be legitimate. Need to correlate to CI/CD job IDs and the backup service.

dave: I see CI job 98321 ran a metrics/export job at 21:11:50 that performs a customer metrics export. It creates a presigned S3 PUT URL and posts to the customer's bucket. The job used our service role to create the presigned URL.

sam: That would explain PUTs into their bucket coming from our fleet IPs. Do we have logs showing presigned URL generation?

lina: Not currently instrumented with tenant/job ids. We have basic audit lines showing the presigned URL call from service account 'backend-exporter' at 2026-03-19T21:11:49, but no linking metadata.

jordan-csm: I've told Acme's security contact we're investigating and asked for their pcap and any presigned URL strings. They're waiting for containment steps.

emma: Containment proposal (quick): 1) Temporarily block outbound S3 egress from tenant-acme-7 for 30 minutes. 2) Snapshot node volumes and container state. 3) Preserve evidence (pcap, flow logs). 4) Hold off on rotating KMS master keys until we confirm scope.

dave: Implementing step 1 and 2 now: disabling outbound to s3 endpoints on the tenant's security group and triggering EBS snapshots of dedicated node instances. Note: this may interrupt legitimate exports.

lina: Agree with holding KMS rotation. Instead, rotate any presigned tokens or credentials that were used by the job (if any). Also, add an alert to appear if presigned URL generation happens for a dedicated tenant.

sec-bot: forensic checklist started: collect container ps, netstat, /var/log/containers/*, kernel audit logs, docker events.

sam: Customer asked for immediate evidence that keys weren't leaked. We should provide the Decrypt event times and the mapping to our deployer role. Also confirm no external IPs besides 18.204.5.12 observed.

emma: CloudTrail shows decrypts from our deployer role. Correlated to CI job 98321. Looks like the job used our role to generate a presigned PUT to the customer's bucket and performed a PUT via that presigned URL. No external actor used their keys.

dave: Root cause hypothesis: export job uses our service role to create presigned URLs for customer buckets. For dedicated tenants with VPC peering that makes it appear as our IPs wrote to their bucket, causing confusion.

jordan-csm: Drafting message to Acme: explain likely cause (internal export job generated presigned URL and uploaded data), actions taken (temporary egress block, snapshots, audit logs collected), and offered remediation options (revoke/rotate presigned tokens, assist with key rotation, provide post-mortem).

emma: Post-incident actions (proposed): 1) Add structured logging for presigned-url generation with tenant id and job id. 2) Default deny egress to customer buckets from dedicated nodes unless explicitly allowed. 3) Add KMS decrypt alert when decrypts originate from our service roles for tenant keys. 4) Runbook updates for customer escalations.

lina: Filing incident ticket INT-2026-042 and adding timeline and artifacts (pcap, cloudtrail extracts, flow logs, snapshots). Assigning to emma,dave,lina.

sec-bot: incident INT-2026-042 created and assigned to emma,dave,lina.

sam: Customer replied acknowledging and will wait for the post-mortem. They want legal cc'd on final comms.

emma: Update after initial forensics: confirmed root cause = internal export job using our service role and presigned URLs. No evidence of unauthorized third-party access or KMS misuse.

dave: Implementing mitigations: disable presigned-url flow for dedicated tenants by default, adding allowlist if export is required. Rolling a config change tonight.

jordan-csm: Customer accepts explanation and requests post-mortem doc + remediation timeline. I'll coordinate with legal and the customer's security team.

lina: Follow-ups added: RBAC review for 'backend-exporter' service role, extend KMS/CloudTrail retention to 90 days for critical keys, instrument presigned-url logs.

sam: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
